executive_summary: U.S. stock futures jumped Monday as the U.S.-Iran ceasefire pause sent crude oil tumbling over 5%, removing the energy-inflation premium that had been driving Fed rate hike bets higher. The FOMC begins its two-day meeting today with markets pricing a 64% chance of a hold at 3.50-3.75%, though the 36% hike probability under Chair Warsh's opaque forward guidance keeps volatility elevated. Four Magnificent Seven companies — Microsoft, Meta, Apple, and Amazon — report earnings this week, creating the most consequential earnings gauntlet of 2026. The semiconductor selloff continues as Asian chipmakers Samsung and SK Hynix tumbled 10%+, but Broadcom bucked the trend on a Samsung partnership announcement, suggesting the correction is positioning-driven rather than fundamental.

macro_events.title: US-Iran Ceasefire Pause Crashes Oil Markets
macro_events.causal_chain: US and Iran pause military strikes after 2 weeks of fighting → oil traders unwind war-risk premium → WTI crashes 5.7% to $84.21, Brent drops to $86.82 → VLCC tanker insurance premiums decline → shipping routes normalize from Cape of Good Hope diversions → airline fuel costs projected to drop 8-12% in Q3 → consumer inflation expectations ease → Treasury yields fall 3bp to 4.65% → Fed hike odds moderate from 42% to 36%
macro_events.geographic_dimension: Middle East, Strait of Hormuz, global shipping lanes, US consumer economy
macro_events.historical_analog: Sep 2019 Abqaiq drone attack — Brent spiked 15% in 24h then fully reversed in 2 weeks as Saudi restored output. This is the mirror image — a war-risk unwind that could partially reverse if negotiations fail.
macro_events.counterargument: Ceasefire is a pause not a peace deal. Iran's nuclear program remains unresolved and re-escalation risk is non-trivial. Oil could spike back to $100+ within days if talks collapse.

macro_events.title: FOMC Meeting Begins — Warsh's Unpredictable Fed
macro_events.causal_chain: Fed Chair Warsh abandoned forward guidance practice → market pricing becomes binary: hold (64%) vs hike (36%) → if hold with hawkish language, DXY stays firm at 101.5, EM currencies stable → if surprise hike to 3.75-4.00%, DXY spikes to 103+, 10Y yield jumps to 4.85%, equity multiples compress 5-8% → cool June CPI (3.5% YoY, core 2.6%) argues for patience, but IMF's 4.7% global inflation forecast keeps hawks engaged
macro_events.geographic_dimension: US monetary policy with global spillovers to EM currencies and risk assets
macro_events.historical_analog: June 2023 skip meeting — Fed held but signaled more hikes ahead, which proved correct with a July 2023 hike. This meeting could be a similar hawkish hold that sets up a September move.
macro_events.counterargument: Oil's 5.7% crash today actually reduces near-term inflation pressure, giving Warsh political cover to hold without sounding dovish. The real data risk is Q3 CPI rebounding from low June base, not July.

affected_tickers.reason: Long-duration bonds lose if hike materializes or hawkish guidance
Banks benefit from NIM expansion on higher rates

macro_events.title: Magnificent Seven Earnings Gauntlet — $12T at Stake
macro_events.causal_chain: MSFT and META report Wednesday, AAPL and AMZN report Thursday → combined market cap ~$12T → AI capex spending revelations will either validate or punish the AI infrastructure trade → Alphabet's -9% last week on capex concerns set a negative template → if MSFT Azure AI revenue shows 50%+ growth, validates the capex cycle → if capex rises without proportional revenue, chip stocks face another leg down → AAPL's restrained AI capex approach was rewarded with +3.5% Friday, suggesting market is rewarding discipline
macro_events.geographic_dimension: US tech sector, global AI supply chain (Taiwan, South Korea, Japan)
macro_events.historical_analog: Q1 2024 Mag 7 earnings season — mixed results led to a 5% Nasdaq correction before recovery over 3 weeks. Current environment has more macro cross-currents from oil and Fed.
macro_events.counterargument: Not all Mag 7 need to be big AI spenders to rally. AAPL's restrained approach was rewarded Friday. The market may be maturing to value AI revenue growth over raw capex spending.

macro_events.title: US-China Tariff Cap at 20% Reduces Uncertainty
macro_events.causal_chain: China Commerce Ministry discloses US pledged to cap replacement tariffs at 20% → below 25-34% levels markets feared → Chinese exporters gain cost visibility → consumer goods inflation in US stabilizes → retail sector benefits from predictable input costs → Xi upcoming US visit suggests further de-escalation → BUT Trump new 12.5% tariffs and simultaneous substantial EU tariff threats show policy remains unpredictable
macro_events.geographic_dimension: US-China bilateral trade, ASEAN supply chain reshoring
macro_events.historical_analog: Phase 1 deal Jan 2020 — markets rallied on trade certainty but gains were short-lived. The 20% cap provides a ceiling but not a floor.
macro_events.counterargument: Trump simultaneously threatening EU with substantial tariffs shows tariff policy is capricious. The 20% cap could be revised upward before Xi visit to extract concessions.

macro_events.title: Semiconductor Selloff Spreads to Asia
macro_events.causal_chain: TSMC earnings beat but raised capex guidance → market interprets spending running ahead of revenue → contagion spreads to Samsung (-10%), SK Hynix (-10%) in Seoul → US chip names hammered Friday: SNDK -11%, INTC/ARM -8%, MRVL/MU -7% → BUT AVGO +2% premarket on Samsung partnership deal → selloff is profit-taking after 47% YTD SOX rally, not fundamental deterioration → BofA raised global semi market forecast to $1.3T
macro_events.geographic_dimension: US, South Korea, Taiwan semiconductor supply chain
macro_events.historical_analog: Q2 2024 chip rotation — SOX corrected 15% from highs before resuming uptrend on Nvidia earnings beat. Current correction follows same pattern of excess positioning being flushed.
macro_events.counterargument: Global semi market forecast raised to $1.3T from $1.0T four months ago. AI GPU demand growing 70%+ YoY. This is a positioning flush, not a secular reversal.
